parts.gloss: the state of what lies within

words.gloss: the nature of what lies buried within

literal: The sprout will reveal what lay hidden in the soil; the words from the mouth will reveal those born in a noble family.
translation: Just as an emerging sprout reveals the nature of the soil in which the seed lay, the words spoken from the mouth reveal the noble lineage of those born to it.
modern: நிலத்தில் புதைந்து கிடக்கும் விதையின் தன்மையை அதிலிருந்து முளைக்கும் முளை காட்டும்; அதுபோல, உயர்ந்த குலத்தில் பிறந்தவர்களின் தன்மையை அவர்கள் வாயிலிருந்து வெளிப்படும் சொல் காட்டும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a beautiful natural analogy to explain how a person's speech reflects their upbringing and lineage. The word 'kāl' here refers to the young sprout or shoot emerging from the earth. Just as the health and type of a sprout reveal the quality of the hidden soil in which the seed lay, the words that come out of a person's mouth instantly reveal the quality and nobility of the family they were born into. The repetition of the verb 'kāṭṭum' (will reveal) emphasizes the direct and inescapable connection between origin and expression.
